harbor_antrieb_executor.summary: On node1 (Alpine 3.23), set up nginx serving HTTPS on port 8443 with a self-signed cert (5-min validity for demonstration) that is auto-renewed by a busybox cron job (every minute, renews when <2min of validity remain) via /usr/local/bin/renew-cert.sh, which atomically replaces cert/key and gracefully reloads nginx (`rc-service nginx reload`) so it picks up the new cert without dropping requests. Verified two live renewals with a continuous HTTPS probe loop showing 100% 200 responses across the cert swap, confirmed both nginx and crond are enabled at boot, restarted node1, confirmed changed boot_id, and confirmed HTTPS plus a third automatic renewal succeeded post-reboot.
actions_performed: Installed nginx, openssl, busybox-openrc, curl on node1 via apk

Created /usr/local/bin/renew-cert.sh: checks cert expiry with openssl x509 -checkend, generates a new 5-minute self-signed cert atomically, logs to /var/log/certrenew/renew.log, and reloads nginx gracefully
Configured /etc/nginx/http.d/ssl-8443.conf to serve HTTPS on 0.0.0.0:8443 using /etc/nginx/ssl/cert.pem and key.pem
Enabled and started nginx (rc-update add nginx default; rc-service nginx start)
Installed a root crontab entry running renew-cert.sh every minute and enabled/started crond
Ran a continuous curl+openssl monitoring loop against $NODE_IP:8443 for ~4.5 minutes to observe a live renewal with zero downtime (68/68 probes returned 200, serial changed mid-loop)
Captured pre-restart baseline (boot_id, uptime, service status, HTTPS 200, cert serial/dates)
Restarted node1 with `reboot` (backgrounded so the ack returned before disconnect)
Polled node1 until exec was available again, confirmed boot_id changed and uptime -s reflects new boot time
Verified nginx and crond auto-started at boot and are enabled in the default runlevel
Confirmed HTTPS still serving 200 post-reboot and waited for a fresh automatic cert renewal to occur, confirming the full renew+reload pipeline persists after restart

evidence.requirement: HTTPS served on port 8443 with a certificate
evidence.summary: nginx config validated, started, listening on 0.0.0.0:8443, curl returns 200 and TLS cert served with matching serial/dates
crond installed with per-minute renewal job; renew.log shows automatic renewal at 09:51:00 (serial changed from 21B27... to 1F57AFC...) without manual intervention

evidence.requirement: Service picks up new certificate while continuing to answer requests (no downtime)
evidence.summary: Continuous monitor loop across the renewal boundary recorded 68/68 HTTP 200 responses with the serving cert serial switching mid-loop, proving graceful nginx reload with zero dropped requests
Captured boot_id 0ede1030..., nginx/crond status started, HTTPS 200, and current cert serial/dates prior to reboot

evidence.requirement: node1 restart acknowledgement and changed boot identity
evidence.summary: Reboot command acknowledged before disconnect; node1 became unreachable then responded again; boot_id changed to 0cc37d0c... (new value) and uptime -s reflects a fresh boot time

evidence.requirement: node1 post-restart recovery of required services and data
evidence.summary: nginx and crond auto-started and enabled at boot; HTTPS returns 200 post-reboot; a further automatic cert renewal (serial 62CB58C8...) occurred via cron after the restart, confirming the renewal pipeline survives a reboot
